title: Berries
source: Piper & Beattie, Flora of the Northwest Coast (1915); Chesnut, Principal Poisonous Plants of the United States (USDA 1898); FM 21-76 Appendix B

questions.question: Growing as: a tree, an upright shrub, a trailing or climbing plant, or a soft-stemmed plant (herb)?
questions.capture_condition: the whole plant is in frame
questions.citation: Piper & Beattie, Flora of the Northwest Coast (1915), habit stated per species description

questions.question: Thorns or prickles on the stems?
questions.capture_condition: a stem section fills the frame up close
questions.citation: Piper & Beattie, Flora of the Northwest Coast (1915), armature stated per species description

questions.question: Leaves on the stem: alternate, opposite, whorled, or all at the base?
questions.capture_condition: a stem with several leaves is in frame
questions.citation: Piper & Beattie, Flora of the Northwest Coast (1915), leaf arrangement per species description

questions.question: Each leaf: one blade (simple), or split into leaflets (compound)?
questions.capture_condition: one full leaf fills the frame
questions.citation: Piper & Beattie, Flora of the Northwest Coast (1915), leaf form per species description

questions.question: The fruit: aggregate (raspberry-like beads), berry (soft, small seeds), drupe (flesh around one stone), or pome (apple-like, seeds in a core)?
questions.capture_condition: a single fruit fills the frame, split open if possible
questions.citation: Piper & Beattie, Flora of the Northwest Coast (1915), fruit form per species description

questions.question: Ripe fruit color?
questions.capture_condition: ripe fruit is in frame in daylight
questions.citation: Piper & Beattie, Flora of the Northwest Coast (1915), fruit color per species description

questions.question: Fruits sit: single or in twos, in a flat-topped cluster, in a long hanging cluster (raceme), or in an umbrella head (umbel)?
questions.capture_condition: a fruiting branch is in frame
questions.citation: Piper & Beattie, Flora of the Northwest Coast (1915), inflorescence per species description

questions.question: Crushed leaf or broken twig: milky sap, a bitter-almond smell, or neither?
questions.citation: Chesnut, Principal Poisonous Plants of the United States (USDA 1898), cherry-laurel and wild cherry hydrocyanic odor
